units.translation: Hermann restored it for δόξαι [opinions]: see under δόξα [opinion]. In Hesychius δόκη : δόκησις [opinion], with faulty accent, if Herodian in Arcadius p. 106, 21 correctly teaches that iambic words in κη that are not contracted, if they have ω in the penult, are accented on the last syllable when they are verbal nouns, πλέκω πλοκή [I weave, weaving], δέκω δοκή [I receive, opinion], ἡ ὑπόνοια [suspicion]. See on Ag. 980.

as in Latin domus, it signifies not only a building, but very often also in a broader sense is said of those who inhabit or have inhabited a house, i.e. of a family. Nor rarely is δόμος or δόμοι said of one's country or paternal home, although this meaning is not in the word itself, but is gathered from the accompanying words, as Ch. 487 πατρώων ἐκ δόμων [from the paternal halls] is placed: about all of which it is said in the Thes. vol. 2 p. 1627.
δόμος and δόμοι are not rarely said of the temples of the gods.
δόμος [house] corrupted from δρόμος [course], which see.
